description:
Problem: .github/workflows/oracle-gate.yml schedules its sweep with cron '41 * * * *' (:35-36); the push trigger (:6-17) runs the sweep only when the gate's policy files change. Scheduled sweeps start 3 to 6 hours apart (2026-10-23T13:46Z to 2026-10-25T12:44Z; the latest pair is 06:46Z then 12:44Z) because GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs. Event-started gate runs are fast, so for these cases the sweep is the long pole:
(a) a gate run that cannot read the PR through REST or GraphQL and has no head posts nothing (docs/internal/oracle-review-v2.md:754-756);
(b) a verdict post job that fails after posting its review but before its dispatch step (oracle-verdict.yml:996-1011), for verdict runs whose completion the bridge cannot map;
(c) resolving the last oracle thread starts no Actions run, leaving a stale failure (merge safety is held by the ruleset's thread-resolution rule; this is a delay);
(d) once the review notification is retired, an edit or dismissal of an oracle review by an account other than the oracle.

Outcome: the sweep also runs on every push to develop, with the cron kept as the fallback for hours without pushes, and a measured bound.

Decision gates:
1. Mechanism (decided): remove the paths filter from the push trigger so every develop push runs the sweep job; keep the cron. The oracle-verdict retry sweep adopts the same trigger in its own workflow; no shared code and no new workflow. A delayed self-dispatch or an external scheduler needs the owner's approval.
2. Cost. From the Actions runs API, record develop pushes per day over the last 7 days and the median and 90th-percentile sweep duration (run_started_at to updated_at) for sweeps since 2026-10-24. Record pushes times median duration. If it exceeds 2 runner-hours a day, get the owner's approval before landing.
3. Concurrency. The existing push-sweep group (oracle-gate.yml:41-42) already keeps one running and the newest pending sweep and never cancels per-PR gates; keep it. If removing the filter changes per-PR grouping, stop and record why.

Item guardrails: no change to the gate decision, the statuses it posts, its concurrency groups, or how per-PR runs are triggered; the sweep remains the only multi-PR evaluator; no new secrets or permissions. oracle-gate.yml is a soundness path, so the PR needs the oracle's review. Land before the retirement of the review notification, which edits the same file and paragraphs.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings in code; commits, PR bodies and docs carry no tracker item IDs or session labels.
